title: Market and limit orders

paragraphs.heading: Order basics
paragraphs.text: A market order prioritizes execution at available order-book prices. A limit order sets a maximum buying price or minimum selling price. A limit order can remain unfilled; it does not guarantee immediate execution.

title: Stop-limit orders

paragraphs.heading: Trigger and fill
paragraphs.text: A stop-limit order has a trigger price and a limit price. Reaching the trigger activates a limit order; it does not guarantee execution. If no matching liquidity is available at the limit price or better, the order can remain unfilled.

title: OCO orders

paragraphs.heading: Linked orders
paragraphs.text: OCO means one cancels the other. Two linked order legs express alternative outcomes. An execution event in one leg can cancel the other according to the exchange rules. Exact supported combinations and cancellation details must be checked against the relevant official documentation.

title: Liquidity and slippage

paragraphs.heading: Execution conditions
paragraphs.text: Liquidity describes how easily an asset can be traded without substantially moving its price. A large market order relative to available order-book depth can consume several price levels and experience slippage.

title: Spread and slippage

paragraphs.heading: Two different concepts
paragraphs.text: The bid-ask spread is the gap between the best bid and best ask. Slippage is the difference between an expected transaction price and the actual execution price. These concepts describe different aspects of execution.

title: Makers and takers

paragraphs.heading: Order-book roles
paragraphs.text: A maker adds resting liquidity to an order book. A taker consumes existing liquidity. A limit order that crosses available opposing orders can act as a taker; the order label alone does not determine its liquidity role.

title: Spot ownership

paragraphs.heading: Spot basics
paragraphs.text: In an unleveraged Spot trade, assets are exchanged using available funds. This differs from borrowing to increase a position. This note does not describe margin collateral, liquidation rules, or derivatives contracts.

title: Base and quote assets

paragraphs.heading: Trading pairs
paragraphs.text: In the illustrative pair BTC/USDT, BTC is the base asset and USDT is the quote asset. The quoted price expresses how much of the quote asset corresponds to one unit of the base asset.

title: Time in force

paragraphs.heading: Order lifetime
paragraphs.text: GTC remains active until filled or cancelled. IOC attempts immediate execution and cancels the unfilled remainder. FOK requires an immediate complete fill or cancellation. These are educational definitions, not live trading instructions.

title: Stablecoins and volatility

paragraphs.heading: Crypto terms
paragraphs.text: A stablecoin is designed to track a reference value, but the design does not guarantee a peg or eliminate risk. Volatility describes the magnitude and speed of price changes. This note provides no current prices or investment recommendations.

title: Order books

paragraphs.heading: Resting bids and asks
paragraphs.text: An order book records resting buy and sell orders at different prices. A bid is an offered buying price; an ask is an offered selling price. Available quantity can vary across price levels.

title: Volume and depth

paragraphs.heading: Market measurements
paragraphs.text: Trading volume measures units exchanged during a time interval. Order-book depth describes available resting quantities at price levels. Historical volume does not by itself specify current depth at every price.
